I love sharing my process, especially with slipcasting, because so many people just aren’t familiar with it. It’s usually not something that gets taught much in pottery or ceramics classes, so there’s a lot of mystery and misconceptions around it. I try to share what I can because this is how I spend most of my days making work, and honestly I find the whole process pretty meditative. There’s such a rhythm to casting, cleaning pieces up, attaching handles, all of it. Carving is definitely still my favorite part though. That’s always the most satisfying for me. Glazing, on the other hand… not my favorite. I save basically all of my glazing until right before a release and then spend one very long week glazing nonstop just to get through everything at once. This green I developed honestly took a while to figure out because green is such an intense pigment. If I add even a little too much into the slip, it stains my molds really badly, which definitely happened during my first round of testing these. So I’ve been slowly adjusting the pigment over time to get it where I want it. And now I’m somehow at the point where I want to make another green. I already have two, so I guess I’m just in a green phase right now, which is funny because green isn’t even my favorite color, it’s Blue. I really don’t know why I’m so obsessed with green lately? Over the last several months I’ve introduced a bunch of new colors, and right now I’m mostly trying to refine how I release work so I can have more pieces available in the same color during each release. For this next one I’m focusing more on greens and reds with a smaller amount of blues mixed in. I’ll keep rotating colors around and doing my best to keep up with what everyone is excited about, which I’m super appreciative of. And obviously I’ll still always be making other pieces too, these are just the ones getting the most attention right now. #pottery #ceramics #handmadeceramics #contemporaryceramics #handcarved

pricing my work is truly my LEAST favourite thing 😭  especially after trying to look closer at the numbers behind my small ceramic business. i’m trying to map out the potential 1, 3, and 5 year revenue and expense projections to see if investing in a kiln and building this business actually makes any sense. at my current $30-$65 price point, i’m losing money selling my work and cannot justify a kiln. i’ve made the terrifying decision to raise my prices by 25-30%. the money will go towards expanding production (investing. in a kiln & shelving), upgrading my website, expanding to ship to the US, and finally, offering private lessons and workshops.  with the price increase, I will still need to survive 6 months - 1 year without a livable wage / making profit. i’ll be focusing on my higher-margin petal bowls and bring in some more affordable $25 products like spoon rests and trinket dishes to keep things as accessible as possible. my mugs are not viable as they take me 2hrs each, but i’m going to keep making them for now and hope i can speed it up. no more lidded jars outside of speciality collections as the margins are too low.  i’m also going to try to secure 1-2 freelance social media clients to provide me with some supplement income as a buffer. this is the behind the scenes of small ceramics business’ that you normally don’t see, because it’s not nearly as cute or fun as the pots themselves. #potterybusiness #ceramics #smallbusiness #priceincrease #handmadeceramics

Maybe part of my own practice right now is learning to care less about Western institutional validation. I can take myself seriously as an artist without believing that a gallery, residency, MFA, collector, or critic makes my work inherently more important than someone making extraordinary pots as their everyday trade. Pottery is ancient, global, utilitarian, and deeply humble. I think a lot of us could stand to remember that.  #pottery #ceramics #wheelthrowing
